summary: Northeast Florida Regional Airport (UST) serves the historic city of St. Augustine, the oldest continuously inhabited European-established settlement in the United States. The airport occupies the site of a former World War II naval air station, originally commissioned as Naval Air Station St. Augustine in 1942. Today it functions primarily as a general aviation facility while also hosting some scheduled commercial service to nearby destinations.
faqs:
Q: How far is Northeast Florida Regional Airport from downtown St. Augustine?
A: The airport is approximately 5 miles north of the historic downtown area, typically a 10-15 minute drive.

Q: Does the airport offer scheduled commercial flights?
A: Yes, the airport has limited scheduled commercial service, but it is best known for general aviation, private flights, and flight training operations.

Q: Is the airport the same one that served as a naval base?
A: Yes, the airfield was originally built as Naval Air Station St. Augustine in 1942 and trained naval aviators during World War II before being converted to civilian use.

Q: Are car rentals available at the airport?
A: Rental car services are available on-site or by arrangement, and several local providers serve the terminal area.
transport_tips: The airport is most easily reached by rental car, as rideshare availability can be limited in this coastal region. US-1 and I-95 both provide quick access from Jacksonville, which is roughly 40 miles to the north. Free parking is generally available on-site for both short-term and extended visits.
local_tip: If you have time between flights, the St. Augustine Lighthouse is just a few miles south of the airport and offers a rewarding climb with panoramic views of the coastline and city.
